# Spark plug replacement

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove intake plenum, take out front passenger side coil pack bolt first for easier spark plug replacement. [t3212]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the intake plenum to gain better access.
2. [Partial] Take out the front passenger side coil pack bolt first, as it is harder to reach.

_Procedure reported by [t3212]._

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Use a spark plug socket with a u-joint and extension bars for tight spaces. [t3212]

## Common mistakes

- Stripping or breaking the coil bolt by trying to screw it back in straight without removing the plenum. [t3212]
- Forgetting that one of two washers might fall into the cylinder while working on the plug. [t3212]
